newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF mission positive about Russia - representative.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission positive about Russia - representative.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund mission which left Moscow last week will make a positive report on Russia, which hopefully will lead to the release of the next quarterly instalment of an IMF loan, a senior fund official said on Monday.

"The mission made a generally positive assessment," resident representative Martin Gilman told Reuters. "Hopefully the board meeting which is due to take place around the beginning of September will also make a positive assessment, which will lead to the release of the next tranche." He added Russia's budgetary position was still a cause for concern.
"The budgetary situation still remains very difficult, particularly the problem of budgetary revenues," Gilman said. This would continue to be problematic and need monitoring.
The fund has repeatedly suspended disbursements of the $10 billion three-year Extended Fund Facility over the past 12 months because of concern about Russia's tax revenues.

But Gilman said the mission found that Russia was almost over-achieving on some other targets in the economic programme backed by the loan, such as the build-up of currency reserves and structural reform.

The fund was also impressed by the determination of the new government team to move ahead in areas such as better monitoring of ministry spending and commitments and the establishment of a new treasury system to handle government payments, he added.
